methodology.dsPowerRole: Tmax, Tmin, Radiation, Rain → Hargreaves ET₀, GDD, FAO-56 daily water balance weather
methodology.dsGpmRole: Rainfall totals, monsoon distribution, dry spells, RUSLE R-factor
methodology.dsSmapRole: 12 monthly root-zone soil moisture percentiles (drought suitability modifier & live dry-spell diagnostics; daily depletion modeled via FAO-56)
methodology.dsGraceProd: JPL Tellus Mascon RL06 V04 CRI
methodology.dsGraceRole: Regional groundwater decline rate (cm/yr) weighted into irrigation & water-stress penalties
methodology.dsNasademRole: Field slope (%) for RUSLE topographic LS-factor & 3D Pedon tilt
methodology.dsFirmsRole: Detection of Oct–Nov crop residue burning to flag status-quo residue management baseline
methodology.dsHlsRole: Savitzky-Golay smoothed NDVI → baseline seasonal crop classification & context history
methodology.dsSoilGridsRole: Sand/silt/clay fractions, pH, bulk density & initial SOC (overridden when farmer SHC lab test is supplied)
methodology.dsMmRole: 4-layer soil moisture (-5 to -150 cm), 5 cm seedbed temperature, blight/hail/fire hazards, 7-day spray/sowing advisory & CMIP6 downscaling
methodology.m01Body: Daily root-zone moisture depletion (TAW, RAW, Ks), evapotranspiration (ETc / ETa), and thermal heat stress simulation. Calibrated against PAU trials: puddled paddy rice requires 175 mm land-soaking and 3.5 mm/day plough-pan percolation; Direct-Seeded Rice (DSR) + AWD uses 75 mm pre-sowing wetting and 2.55 mm/day percolation on loam, saving 24–28% irrigation water.
methodology.m02Body: 5 soil carbon pools (DPM, RPM, BIO, HUM, IOM) following Coleman & Jenkinson (1996) and Falloon et al. (1998). Simulates 10-year SOC trajectory as modified by soil temperature, moisture, clay content, and vegetative cover. Residue retention adds active DPM/RPM inputs; stubble burning reduces carbon retention to ~10% ash.
methodology.m03Body: Seasonal N mass balance factoring synthetic fertilizer input, symbiotic biological nitrogen fixation (BNF) by grain and cover legumes, atmospheric deposition (10 kg N/ha/yr), and grain harvest removal. Preceding legumes credit 25 kg N/ha synthetic fertilizer reduction to successor crops.
methodology.m04Body: Composite 0–100 index mapping rotation practices onto: (1) Minimise disturbance, (2) Maximise soil cover, (3) Maximise living roots, (4) Maximise biodiversity (Shannon botanical index), and (5) Integrate livestock/green manure, combined with 10-year SOC trajectory and RUSLE soil erosion score.
methodology.m05Body: Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation (A = R·K·LS·C·P) using Renard rainfall erosivity (R), Williams (1995) topsoil erodibility (K), NASADEM 30 m slope length/steepness (LS), and rotation-specific canopy cover (C).
methodology.m06Body: Gross margins calculated from official Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices (CACP) Minimum Support Prices (MSP), PAU Cost of Cultivation reports, ISU Ag Decision Maker, UC Davis Cost Studies, and Tegemeo/ICRISAT benchmarks.
methodology.sfHeatBody: High temperatures (>32 °C) during wheat grain-fill (1 March to 15 April) deactivate starch synthase and shorten duration, reducing yields by ~1.8% per degree-day above 32 °C. TerraLoop explicitly tracks average days exceeding this threshold and models -1.0 °C canopy cooling from Happy Seeder mulch.
methodology.sfRainBody: Satellite reanalysis series may feature artificial decadal shifts. TerraLoop enforces a strict filter on automated trend advisory notes: only trends between 10% and 30% are reported; spurious step-change anomalies (>30%) are suppressed.
methodology.lim1: NASA POWER resolution is ~50 km; micro-climatic terrain variations are not captured.
methodology.lim2: NASA SMAP (9 km) and GRACE (~300 km native) provide regional hydro-climatic context rather than sub-field resolution.
methodology.lim3: Soil properties derive from ISRIC SoilGrids 250 m digital soil mapping; local laboratory soil tests should override modeled values when available.
methodology.lim4: Simulated yields assume recommended standard fertilizer application and disease control guidelines.
